stem: What is a Knowledge article?

options.text: A trusted piece of information such as a how-to or fix
A support case that records a customer's problem
A report that lists the most common case reasons
A permission set that lets agents edit cases

explanation: Knowledge articles are approved answers that agents and customers can search.

stem: How does Lightning Knowledge store different kinds of articles, such as FAQ and How-to?

options.text: As record types on a single Knowledge object
As separate objects for each type

explanation: Lightning Knowledge uses one Knowledge object, and you create different article types with record types.

stem: Which feature license do users need to create and manage Knowledge articles?
explanation: The Knowledge User feature license is needed to author and manage articles.

stem: What is the usual lifecycle of a Knowledge article?
explanation: Articles start as drafts, are published for users, and are archived when they are out of date.

stem: A published article needs a correction. What should the author do?

options.text: Edit it to create a new version, then publish

explanation: Editing a published article creates a new version that is published after review.

stem: Which feature controls which users can see which articles, using a folder-like hierarchy?
explanation: Data categories organise articles and control visibility by user or role.

stem: Which feature controls where an article is published, such as internal app or customer?
explanation: Channels decide whether an article is available internally, to partners, customers or the public.

stem: Which feature decides the type and layout of an article, such as FAQ or Troubleshooting?
explanation: Record types on the Knowledge object define article types and layouts.

stem: An agent wants to send the customer an approved answer while working a case. What should they do?

options.text: Search and attach a Knowledge article to the case
Write a new answer each time from scratch
Create a new queue for the approved answers
Merge the case with the customer's last case

explanation: Agents can search for articles in the case page and attach or send them.

stem: What does Omni-Channel do?

options.text: Routes work such as cases and chats to available agents
Creates and schedules reports for service managers
Imports case data from spreadsheets into Salesforce
Controls which users can log in to the service console

explanation: Omni-Channel pushes work to agents based on capacity, presence and routing rules.

stem: What does an agent's presence status tell Omni-Channel?

options.text: Whether the agent is available to receive work
The agent's profile, which sets their object permissions
The agent's role in the hierarchy, which sets their reports
The agent's licence type, which sets their feature access

explanation: Presence statuses such as Available or On Break control when work can be routed to the agent.

stem: What does capacity control in Omni-Channel?

options.text: How much work an agent can handle at once
How many cases a customer can open

explanation: Capacity defines the number of work items an agent can carry at the same time.

stem: Which Omni-Channel feature matches work to agents who have specific expertise?
explanation: Skills-based routing routes work to agents with the required skills.

stem: Agents are not receiving routed cases. What should you check first?

options.text: Queue, routing configuration, service channel and agent presence
The case page layout and which fields appear on it
The sharing rule that lets agents see all closed cases
The email template used in the auto-response rule

explanation: Omni-Channel needs a queue, routing configuration, service channel and a presence status that allows work.

stem: Which channel lets customers chat with an agent in a web or in-app window?
explanation: Messaging connects chat on web, in-app and messaging apps to Salesforce.

stem: Which Salesforce site offers customers a branded self-service portal with knowledge and cases?
explanation: Experience Cloud sites let customers and partners log in and help themselves.

stem: Customers keep asking the same question. What is the best long-term fix?

options.text: Write a Knowledge article and publish it on a help site
Hire more agents so every customer gets a fast reply
Build a new object that stores every repeated question
Escalate every repeated case so a manager handles it

explanation: Knowledge reduces repeat contacts and helps customers solve problems themselves.

stem: What is self-service deflection?

options.text: Customers solving problems themselves without creating a case
Escalating a case to a manager when an agent cannot solve it quickly
Merging two cases that came from the same customer into one
Routing cases to a queue so a skilled agent can take them

explanation: Deflection is when customers find the answer on their own, reducing case volume.

stem: Which metric measures customer happiness after a service interaction?
explanation: Customer satisfaction scores come from surveys after service.

stem: A known fault affects hundreds of customers. Which pair helps the team handle it efficiently?

options.text: A parent case with linked child cases, and a knowledge article
A new profile and a role for the support team
A new price book and a quote for the customers
A sandbox and a change set for the fix

explanation: Link the reports to one parent case and give agents and customers one article to use.

stem: Cases must be routed automatically to available agents based on capacity. Which feature fits?
explanation: Omni-Channel pushes work to agents based on presence and capacity.
